newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks rise marginally by close.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks rise marginally by close.

text.p: Despite several bouts of profit-taking, Thai stocks closed slightly up in moderate trade on Wednesday as investors bought communication and banking issues for short-term speculation, brokers said.

"The market moved sluggishly throughout the day because of investor worries about the asset quality of finance firms. An announcement of Finance One that it was in talks with creditors worsened the market mood," said Thanawat Patchimkul of Seamico Securities.
The composite SET index finished 2.90 points up to 496.03 on 5.2 billion baht turnover.
Finance counters continued to fall on Wednesday, declining 4.82 percent and was third-ranked in terms of value.
Investor worries over the sector came after a senior finance executive's private estimate on Monday that up to 31.5 percent of total finance firm loans could be classified non-performing.
The announcement by Finance One that it was in talks with foreign creditors to discuss repayment of debts worth about $46.4 million induced investors to further dump finance issues, brokers said.
Brokers said investors were also awaiting for key economic indicators to be released by the central bank on Thursday.
The SET-50 index rose 0.37 point to 35.27.
The banking sector was first-ranked in terms of value, falling 0.23 percent, followed by the communication sector, which gained 3.50 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank fell one baht to 77, BEC World, operator of a television station, gained five to 204, and Advanced Info advanced 16 to 178.
Brokers said the market was expected to be quiet on Thursday as investors awaited the release of key economic indicators to be released in the afternoon.
